transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is that I keep forgetting really basic adult-life things, and it’s not just annoying anymore—it’s starting to actually cost me things.

Like, I’ll forget to pay a bill even though I know it exists, or I’ll see an interview email and think, “I need to respond to that,” and then somehow days go by and I haven’t. Or I’ll miss appointments because I didn’t remember until after, or I’ll start an errand and not actually follow through with it. It’s embarrassing because these are things I feel like I should be able to handle, especially after finishing college, but it keeps happening.

And now it feels bigger than just being forgetful, because I’ve missed opportunities—like actual interview-related stuff—and I’m worried I’m messing up my future because I can’t stay on top of basic responsibilities. That’s why I’m here.

Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with forgetfulness, staying organized, or following through on tasks back in childhood or your school years, or is this something that really started later on?

No, it definitely goes way back. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way when I was little, obviously, but looking back it was very much a thing even in elementary school.

Teachers would write these comments like, “She’s bright,” or “She understands the material,” but then there would always be a “but” after it—like I was constantly losing worksheets, or I’d forget to turn in something I had actually done, or my desk was just… honestly kind of a disaster. Like I remember opening it and there would be crumpled papers and old assignments and random stuff, and I couldn’t find the thing the teacher was asking for even if it was supposedly right there.

I also remember getting in trouble for rushing through directions. I’d just start the assignment because I thought I knew what we were doing, and then I’d realize I missed some key instruction. And I talked out of turn a lot, too—not trying to be rude, I just felt like if I had the thought I had to say it right then or it would disappear.

So yeah, it’s not like this suddenly appeared after college. The adult consequences are worse now, but the pattern was there really early.

Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have to be moving—needing to get up, tap your foot, or feeling like you're 'driven by a motor'—especially in situations where you're expected to sit still?

Yeah, very much. That’s actually one of the things I notice the most in situations where I’m supposed to just sit there and be normal.

Like if I’m in an interview, or a meeting, or even just watching a movie with someone, I get this feeling inside my body that’s hard to describe. It’s not just “I’m bored.” It’s more like this pressure building up, like I need to move or shift or do something with my hands, or I feel like I’m going to crawl out of my skin. I’ll be trying so hard to sit still and look attentive, but inside I’m thinking about how badly I want to get up, change positions, tap my foot, play with a pen, anything.

And the worse part is that I’m usually very aware that I’m doing it, especially in formal situations. So then I’m spending energy trying to control the fidgeting, but that almost makes the restless feeling louder, if that makes sense. Like sitting still feels physically uncomfortable after a while, not just mentally annoying.

Aside from the restlessness we just talked about, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like your health, finances, or relationships—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I don’t think so—not in that kind of constant, across-everything way.

I mean, I definitely worry when something is actively going wrong, or when I realize I forgot something important and then I’m like, “Oh my god, what did I mess up?” But it doesn’t feel like I’m just sitting around most days worrying about my health or relationships or finances for no reason. It’s more tied to specific things when they come up.

I guess I can get stressed about consequences, but I wouldn’t say I’m generally anxious about a bunch of different areas all the time. At least, I haven’t really noticed that as the main issue.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I’ve been persistently sad in the way you’re asking, like crying all the time or feeling this heavy sadness every day.

And I don’t think I’ve totally lost interest in things, either. I mean, sometimes I don’t get around to things I enjoy, or I’ll put them off and then feel kind of blah about everything, but it’s hard for me to tell if that’s the same as losing pleasure. If I actually start something I like, I can usually still enjoy it.

So… over the past couple weeks, I wouldn’t say there’s been this clear depressed mood or loss of interest that’s been the main thing. It’s more that my mood can get affected by how the day is going, if that makes sense.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a lifelong pattern (since elementary school) of inattentive symptoms—losing items, incomplete tasks, disorganization, forgetfulness, missing key instructions—alongside hyperactive-impulsive symptoms—internal restlessness, need to move, blurting out thoughts, and discomfort with sitting still in structured settings. Both symptom clusters are present, persistent since childhood, and currently cause functional impairment in adult responsibilities (missed bills, missed interviews, incomplete errands). Anxiety (GAD) and depressive symptoms were explicitly screened for and denied as primary drivers of the current presentation, making combined-type ADHD the best fit over an anxiety or mood disorder explanation.
